hook: Rational points on Cayley's cubic surface grow like B(log B)^6, matching Peyre's prediction.
summary: Counting rational points of bounded height on the four-nodal Cayley cubic surface, with its nine lines removed, gives N(B) asymptotic to a Peyre constant times B(log B)^6. The proof parametrizes by universal torsors and combines lattice counting with Poisson summation. The result holds for the open subset only and for the maximum-coordinate height.
title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
